claims.text: A predictive approach incorporating atomic size mismatch and local chemical ordering will accurately identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity variants of the CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy.
Alloys above a critical threshold in atomic misfit and local chemical ordering will exhibit at least 25% lower phonon thermal conductivity than predicted by traditional composition-based models.
Systematic changes in elemental fractions can produce a range of atomic size mismatch and chemical short-range-order characteristics in Cantor-alloy variants.
Maintaining a consistent microstructure would make observed conductivity differences arise primarily from composition and local bonding environments.
Atomic size mismatch and local chemical ordering jointly influence local vibrational and bonding environments.
Increased atomic size mismatch introduces spatial variation in bonding environments.
Enhanced local chemical order introduces spatial variation in bonding environments.
Spatially varying bonding environments disrupt phonon modes and increase phonon scattering.
Increased phonon scattering reduces phonon thermal conductivity.
Cantor-alloy variants above the proposed threshold will consistently have at least 25% lower thermal conductivity than baseline composition-based predictions.
Only alloys above the proposed threshold will meet the low-thermal-conductivity criterion.
Traditional composition-based heuristics do not explicitly include atomic-misfit or local-chemical-order descriptors.
The predictive approach is applicable only within the studied Cantor-alloy compositional range at room temperature and under minimized microstructural variation.
Applicability to other high-entropy-alloy systems, high temperatures, or regimes dominated by additional scattering mechanisms is uncertain.
